value.rationale: The squared path is a canonical chordal family with overlapping triangles and graph diameter growing with n. Its finite-dimensional real Lipschitz-free unit balls have a natural but nontrivial facet invariant. The exact all-dimensional generating function, recurrence, and classification of saturated-edge boundary transitions supply a structural result beyond textbook simplex/cross-polytope cases and outside the bipartite edge-gluing multiplication law. This exact enumerative fact is useful as a benchmark for metric-Banach polytope geometry and avoids arbitrary parameter slices.
